summary: Confirm that accepted moves follow stored edges, including level changes, and that hints are computed or reported unavailable.
objective: Every accepted move and every hint step corresponds to an edge of the stored graph at its recorded revision.
applies_when: Movement is constrained to an authored graph rather than to free space.
The projection can make unconnected cells look adjacent.
The interface offers hints or automatic paths.
intent_signals: it let me walk through a wall that looked open
example_prompts: Check that moves in this layered maze follow the stored graph.

principles: The traversable graph is authoritative: two cells that look adjacent in projection are not connected unless an edge says so.
Level changes are ordinary edges of a declared kind, and treating them as a special case invites moves that no edge supports.

A hint is either a computed path over that graph or an honest unavailable, and the two unavailable reasons are different: a completed search that found no path means unreachable, while an exhausted budget or a paused search means undetermined.
implementation: Store cells and edges explicitly, including inter-level links, and route every accepted move through an edge lookup.
Attempt moves that are geometrically adjacent but unlinked, and moves across a level boundary with and without a link.
Compute reachability from start to goal before publishing the instance and record the result together with the graph revision it was computed from.

When a hint is requested compute the path with a documented search over the same graph, including its neighbour and tie-break rule, and record the path with its length; if the search completes without a path, report unreachable, and if it stops on a budget, report undetermined.
observable_checks: Every accepted move corresponds to an edge in the stored graph; a move without an edge names the projection that misled the input layer.
The path history is a walk in the graph, so consecutive entries are always linked and each undo removes one step under the declared history policy.

A hint either reproduces a path that the same search with the same declared tie rule finds over the current graph, or reports unreachable or undetermined with the reason; a different path of equal validity is not a defect unless exact path equality was declared, but a path the search cannot reproduce at all is removed.

known_limits: Checks movement and hint provenance over an authored graph; it does not evaluate maze quality or claim minimal solutions.
Authored verification guidance; no maze implementation was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.
